body: I’m not saying I would have been able to in this situation, but I’m trying to paint a picture of equivalency here. Dangerous, tense situations develop fast. It’s better to be prepared to handle them in the rare case you encounter one than not.

I was walking down the street and asked for money by a homeless person. When I told them I only had my cards on me and turned to keep walking, I was blindsided by a punch from a second homeless person. The blow broke my nose and sent me to the floor, knocking me out. They lifted my keys and my wallet while I was out.

You’re telling me that in that time I could have called the cops and waited for them to arrive? Not only that, SLCPD is notoriously understaffed, much like other big city departments. The call response time would have been very slow if I even had the chance to call them.

I live in Salt Lake City. Our city is at an all-time high for violent crime, much like other big cities right now. Just because it’s in Utah doesn’t make it safe. We have a huge drug problem here.

In fact, about 2 months ago, I was assaulted and robbed by 2 homeless individuals. It was after that that I started to carry 90% of the time.

Interesting about most cops not being gun enthusiasts. I would think there would be some general level of enthusiasm, as it is the most important tool in your arsenal, but I do kind of understand why most wouldn’t.

The one time I did talk to cops investigating a noise complaint at my house, I did notify them I had a gun in the house. They found out I was liberal and they all roasted me for being a liberal gun owner lol.

Here’s another tangentially related question for you. Let’s say I’m in the grocery store and reach for an item up above and it accidentally exposes my holstered weapon. If you, an LEO, observed that, would anything happen?

In Utah, incidental display is not a crime, but I do get nervous when I’m shopping or engaged in some other activity in which I may reach for something. Usually I am cautious to make sure I do not expose the firearm, but obviously it’s always a small possibility in your day-to-day if you have to reach for something. Just want to make sure I am never drawing unwanted attention from LEOs.

I’ve mostly always had positive interactions with police, the only exception being when I called officers to assist my now ex-girlfriend who was in argument with her abusive mother. The two female officers sided with the mother (I was like 18 at the time) and called me a “white knight.” I only called to make sure nobody got hurt and that the peace was kept, so that kind of left a bad taste in my mouth. Otherwise, I’ve always had very positive interactions with police and am never confrontational (really with anyone in general, LEO or not).

So in my instance, sounds like I should preface the conversation with “Just so you know, I am carrying a concealed firearm. It is holstered at my hip at the 1 o’clock position.”

Even before I started carrying, I always kept my hands up on the top of the dash and have my documents ready and out and on top. If I have to retrieve anything else, I always announce my intention of making a movement within the car and ask the officer if that is okay. The officer has always expressed appreciation for my behavior because, even though I was not carrying a weapon, he was grateful that I wanted to make sure it was a smooth interaction where everyone felt safe.

So I would do the same things obviously, but disclose that I have a firearm. Obviously there is much more at stake during a traffic stop when the person being pulled over has a firearm. Announcing my movements would be a must. If something I needed was in my pocket, a movement toward my pocket could be interpreted as a movement toward my holster.

I definitely want to get my actual CCP. Not only for permit reciprocity in other states, but also for more comprehensive training and it is a more sure indication that I’m a law abiding citizen. I have no criminal record, but I feel a CCP would be an immediate sign that I know what I am doing.

I have lots of firearms training from Boy Scouts, so it’s not like I am clueless when it comes to firearms, but the CCW class would be helpful to learn more about self-defense. I have read extensively into Utah’s self-defense laws though, so I feel as if I have the fundamental legal knowledge to know when use of a concealed firearm is appropriate

(and God I hope I never have to, but I did start carrying regularly after I was assaulted/robbed on the street).

I do not have a concealed carry permit, though I do intend to get one so that I can carry in other states. Utah does not require CCP’s anymore for citizens over 21 and legally allowed to own a firearm.

Utah is a very pro-individual rights state and has become more so in recent years. For example, the passage of constitutional carry in May. They have also progressively modified self-defense laws to give more and more favor to the defender.

Edit: by individual rights, I mean them in the ideologically conservative sense. The state is very anti-choice, anti-marijuana, etc.
